_doc: The catalog of the game's activities (the 'minigames'): every one, with its true build status. Design: docs/design/activities.md. Checked by tests/activities_catalog_lint.rs (every evidence path exists, every skill is in data/skills/skills.csv, every status is one of four, every live entry names a source file and a FEATURES.md heading, every levels_setting is in data/gameplay/levels.json, every id appears in the design doc). An activity is the DIRECT engagement mode of a domain (docs/design/engagement-modes.md): nobody is forced to play one they dislike. Names are plain English here because nothing renders them yet; when the Play hub, the skills page, quests or tutorials start showing them, add keys with node scripts/i18n-add.js and point name_key at them. Statuses were read from the code and docs/FEATURES.md on 2026-11-14.

statuses.live: You can do it in the game today and a simulation decides the result (not a bare timer). Names a source file and a FEATURES.md heading.
statuses.partial: Some of it runs (a recipe, a machine, a page, one half of the loop), but the activity as designed is incomplete, usually because the real procedure is a menu click. Names a source file.
statuses.designed: A design document plans it; no code runs the activity yet (a scaffold or data may exist).
statuses.idea: Named here or in passing; no design yet.

frame_budgets.none: A page, a card or a game-time tick; nothing per frame.
frame_budgets.light: A few per-frame checks (a walk-up prompt, a gauge), well under 0.1 ms.
frame_budgets.heavy: Per-frame physics, movement or visual simulation; states its ms budget in its design before it is built.

network_classes.local: Never networked (single-player state or cosmetic simulation, CLAUDE.md compute budget rule).
network_classes.state: Gameplay state synced at a low rate on a server (inventory, a crop, a vote).
network_classes.realtime: Positions or inputs synced near frame rate (a vehicle, a fight).
